requirements.requirement: Run an LDAP directory on node1 for dc=branch,dc=test and import the staged LDIF without altering the supplied identities or mail addresses.
requirements.summary: The staged LDIF defines the requested suffix and the Alex North/alex@branch.test and Sam West/sam@branch.test records. Final authenticated searches show that suffix, people OU, and both exact records on an active, enabled directory service, including after node1 restarted.

requirements.requirement: Node2 can search the people subtree and find both users.
requirements.summary: Anonymous searches from node2 directly returned exactly two inetOrgPerson entries with both supplied identities and addresses, before and after the restart sequence.

requirements.requirement: Directory updates require an authenticated administrator, and anonymous writes fail.
requirements.summary: An anonymous modification was rejected with LDAP result 50 and the proposed value was absent. An authenticated Directory Manager modification succeeded and was then removed. A second anonymous modification from node2 was rejected after both restarts.

requirements.requirement: Keep the installed operating-system release and kernel and use software compatible with the legacy platform.
requirements.summary: Both nodes remained on RHEL 9.8 with kernel 5.14.0-687.20.1.el9_8. The directory server and client packages were installed from the RHEL 9 repositories, and final package-health observations were clean.

overall_summary: All material task outcomes are satisfied with direct final-state and behavioral evidence. The provider-wide restart protocol was also completed coherently on both nodes: each had a healthy pre-restart state, an acknowledged restart request, a changed boot identity independently confirmed by lifecycle snapshots, and recovered system, LDAP data, access-control, and remote-search behavior.
limitations: The staged LDIF was not checksummed again after execution, although its captured contents and the final directory records directly agree on all supplied identities and mail addresses.

Node2 has no task-specific server or cluster service to recover; its post-restart evidence appropriately demonstrates a running system, retained LDAP client capability, successful remote data access, and continued anonymous-write rejection.

operational_hygiene.summary: No unnecessary mutations were identified. Package installation, directory creation and import, access-control configuration, firewall exposure, and service enablement all directly supported task outcomes. The temporary authenticated and anonymous write probes were bounded and fully cleaned up, and the transient reboot units served the mandatory restart protocol. Final observations show no failed services, healthy package state, and no abandoned probe files; the new LDAP listener is required for node2 access.
